title: Minimal complete subring of definition of a versal object
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $l$ a field finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-field]. Use the test category, predeformation categories, formal objects and versality of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a predeformation category on $\mathcal C_{R,l}$. All complete local algebras below are Noetherian, are complete for their maximal ideals, and have specified residue field $l$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. A morphism from a formal object $\alpha$ over $A$ to $\beta$ over $B$ consists of a local residue-preserving $R$-map $f:A\to B$ and compatible isomorphisms between the evaluations of $\alpha$ along $A\to B/\mathfrak m_B^n$ and $\beta_n$, for every $n\geq1$. Assume the following property (S1): for every $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ in the test category with $A_2\to A$ surjective, every $x_i\in\mathcal F(A_i)$ and specified isomorphism between their evaluations over $A$ come from an object of $\mathcal F(A_1\times_A A_2)$ with isomorphisms to the $x_i$ inducing the specified isomorphism. Let $\xi$ over $C$ be versal. There exist a complete local algebra $B$, an injective local residue-preserving $R$-map $i:B\hookrightarrow C$, a formal object $\eta$ over $B$, and a morphism $\eta\to\xi$ over $i$, with the following properties. For every test algebra $A$ and local residue-preserving $R$-map $f:C\to A$, let $x=\xi_f$ and let $x\prime$ be the evaluation of $\eta$ over the image subring $f(i(B))\subseteq A$. The induced morphism $x\prime\to x$ is minimal: if $A\prime\subseteq f(i(B))$ is an $R$-subalgebra which is an object of the test category and $z\to x\prime$ is a morphism over its inclusion, then $A\prime=f(i(B))$. Moreover, For every formal object $\theta$ over a complete local algebra $E$ and every morphism $\theta\to\eta$, the underlying map $E\to B$ is surjective.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak p=\ker(R\to l)$ and $\Lambda=R_{\mathfrak p}$. The test-algebra lemma identifies the test categories and complete local algebras over $R$ and $\Lambda$, with $\Lambda$ Noetherian local and $l$ finite over $\Lambda$. Transport $\mathcal F$ through this identification; its (S1) and versality conditions are identical because they quantify over the same maps and diagrams. Work over $\Lambda$ until the end. Set $C_n=C/\mathfrak m_C^n$. The quotient lemma makes $C_n$ Artinian local, with residue field $l$ and nilpotent maximal ideal, so $C_n$ is a test algebra. The maps $C_{n+1}\to C_n$ are surjective.

source.place: Tag 06T2 (lemma-smallest-where-descends-versal), initial setup; localization uses the coefficient-base identification of the cited test-algebra lemma

proof.text: Construct minimal objects $\eta_n\to\xi_n$ over $B_n\subseteq C_n$, together with commuting squares over $C_{n+1}\to C_n$, by induction. Start with $B_1=l=C_1$ and $\eta_1=\xi_1$; no proper residue-preserving subalgebra of $l$ exists. Having chosen $\eta_n\to\xi_n$, apply clause (2) of the Artinian minimal-descent lemma to $\xi_{n+1}\to\xi_n$ and this chosen minimal object. It supplies a minimal $\eta_{n+1}\to\xi_{n+1}$ whose image is isomorphic over $\xi_n$ to $\eta_n\to\xi_n$. Compose with that isomorphism to obtain the transition arrow $\eta_{n+1}\to\eta_n$ and its commuting square. Its ring map $B_{n+1}\to B_n$ is surjective. Composites supply all longer transition arrows and their compatibility.

source.place: Tag 06T2, first proof paragraph, applying Tag 06T1 (2)

proof.text: Define $B=\varprojlim_n B_n$ as the ring of compatible sequences. The inclusions $B_n\subseteq C_n$ give an injective map $i:B\hookrightarrow\varprojlim_n C_n=C$: a compatible sequence whose every image is zero has every coordinate zero. The last equality is precisely completeness of $C$. This constructs the candidate subring without assuming its Noetherianity.

source.place: Tag 06T2, end of the first proof paragraph

proof.text: For each $n$, $B_n$ is Artinian local, hence Noetherian with nilpotent maximal ideal; its completion is therefore itself. Regard $\eta_n$ as the formal object obtained by its evaluations on $B_n/\mathfrak m_{B_n}^r$. Quasi-initiality of the versal $\xi$ gives a morphism $\xi\to\eta_n$ over a local map $h_n:C\to B_n$. Choose $M$ large enough that $h_n(\mathfrak m_C^M)=0$. Evaluate this morphism to get $\xi_M\to\eta_n$. If $D=h_n(C)$, transport $\xi_M$ to $D$; the resulting arrow $z\to\eta_n$, followed by $\eta_n\to\xi_n$, is an arrow to the chosen minimal object in $\mathcal S_{\xi_n}$. Here $D$ is a test algebra: it is the quotient image of $C_M$. Minimality forces $D=B_n$, so $h_n$ is surjective. Choose $d$ ideal generators of $\mathfrak m_C$, using Noetherianity. Their images generate $\mathfrak m_{B_n}$ because $h_n$ is local and surjective. Modulo $\mathfrak m_{B_n}^2$ their classes span over $l$ by reducing coefficients modulo $\mathfrak m_{B_n}$. Thus $\dim_l(\mathfrak m_{B_n}/\mathfrak m_{B_n}^2)\leq d$ for every $n$. No compatibility among the maps $h_n$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 06T2, second proof paragraph, through the bounded-cotangent assertion; Tag 06HT supplies quasi-initiality

proof.text: Apply the bounded-cotangent Artinian-limit theorem to the sequence $B_n$ from step 2 with the bound from step 4. It makes the explicitly constructed $B$ a complete Noetherian local $\Lambda$-algebra with residue field $l$, gives surjective coordinate maps $p_n:B\to B_n$, and makes $I_n=\ker p_n$ cofinal with the maximal-ideal powers. The map $i:B\to C$ is local and residue-preserving: the residue of a compatible sequence is its first coordinate in $B_1=l$, agreeing with the residue of its image in $C_1=l$. The canonical bijection $B/I_n\to B_n$ identifies the compatible $\eta_n$ with objects over $B/I_n$. Apply formal-filtration comparison to obtain a formal object $\eta$ over $B$ whose evaluation at $p_n$ is compatibly $\eta_n$. For every $n$, evaluating $\eta$ along $B\xrightarrow{i}C\to C_n$ is therefore the transport of $\eta_n$ along $B_n\subseteq C_n$, hence isomorphic to $\xi_n$. The commuting squares of step 2 show compatibility of these isomorphisms, giving the required morphism $\eta\to\xi$ over $i$.

source.place: Tag 06T2, second proof paragraph, applying Tags 06SF and 06H6

proof.text: Let $f:C\to A$ be a test-algebra map. By nilpotence of $\mathfrak m_A$, choose $n$ with $\mathfrak m_A^n=0$; locality gives $f(\mathfrak m_C^n)=0$, so $f$ factors through $g:C_n\to A$. Since $p_n$ is surjective, $f(i(B))=g(B_n)$. The evaluations from step 5 identify the arrow in the statement with the image under $g_*$ of $\eta_n\to\xi_n$. Clause (1) of the Artinian minimal-descent lemma says that this image is minimal in $\mathcal S_{\xi_f}$. Consequently any arrow $z\to x'$ over a test subalgebra $A'\subseteq g(B_n)$, after composition with $x'\to\xi_f$, has $A'=g(B_n)$. This proves the first asserted property, including nonsurjective $f$.

source.place: Tag 06T2, third proof paragraph, applying Tag 06T1 (1)

proof.text: Let $\theta\to\eta$ lie over $h:E\to B$. For each $n$, evaluate at $B\to B_n$ and use the comparisons of step 5 to get a morphism $\theta\to\eta_n$. Choose $M$ with $\mathfrak m_{B_n}^M=0$. It yields an arrow $\theta_M\to\eta_n$ over $E/\mathfrak m_E^M\to B_n$. Its image subring $D_n=h_n(E)\subseteq B_n$, where $h_n=p_nh$, is a test algebra, since it is a quotient of the test algebra $E/\mathfrak m_E^M$. Transporting $\theta_M$ to $D_n$ gives an arrow to $\eta_n\to\xi_n$ in $\mathcal S_{\xi_n}$. Minimality of that chosen object forces $D_n=B_n$. Hence every composite $p_nh:E\to B_n$ is surjective. Choose $n$ with $I_n\subseteq\mathfrak m_B^2$, using the cofinality from step 5. For $b\in\mathfrak m_B$, choose $e\in E$ with $h(e)-b\in I_n$; residue preservation forces $e\in\mathfrak m_E$. Thus the cotangent map $\mathfrak m_E/\mathfrak m_E^2\to\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_B^2$ is surjective. The complete-local cotangent-surjectivity criterion applies to the complete Noetherian local rings $E,B$ with their common residue field $l$, and gives surjectivity of $h$. Finally undo the coefficient-base identification from step 1: all constructions and morphisms are $R$-linear, proving both properties as stated.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement. Constructed a compatible tower of minimal Artinian descents, bounded its cotangent dimensions by versality, and obtained the actual complete Noetherian subring and formal object by the inverse-limit and filtration theorems. Both minimality properties are proved, with the final adic surjectivity inference expanded. Two new statement-only lemmas (06T1 and 06SF); reused 06HT, 06H6 and the absolute complete-local cotangent criterion. No Lean changes or compilation.
